[A786] TAKEN
Branch: `920-save-burst` (from `dev-soft-core` `659d7687`)
Authoritative references: #920; #665 issuecomment-6899519003 (finding 13, the "B" finding of the report) and the ruling #665 issuecomment-6899740728, item 1 (target, allowed and refused mechanisms) and item 4 (no pass carries both a store step and a PHY poll slice; this lane syncs onto #919's review head); Milan v1.2 5.3.13; `sw/firmware/ctrl_nvm/nvm_store.c`/`.h` (DR2a first-dirty window, DR2c attempts and back-off), `sw/firmware/ctrl/aecp/aecp_nvm.c`, `sw/firmware/ctrl/plat/ctrl_plat.c` and `sw/firmware/ctrl/loop/ctrl_loop.h` (THE STEP), `docs/design/SPLIT_CONTROL_MEMORY.md` sections 12 and 13 (the save's windows and worst cases).
Interpreted scope: prove the cause before any fix: replay the burst (entity, group and every user-settable object name, paced as a controller sends them, a cut 10 s after the last response) in the save harness at 1x1/1if and 8x8/1if, and on the board against its current image (no reflash) with the store's state read over the console before the cut; test a failed attempt inside the back-off, the flash part's erase/program time and the capture's `taken` rule as well as the step rate. Then fix the cause found as that defect, and only by the ruling's allowed mechanisms, so every acknowledged change is durable within 5 s of its response at both shapes under the contract's held load, a burst marking every name and a change marked during a save in flight included. No change to the step's length, the age limit, the tiers, the pace, the two-slot sequence, the blank check, the verify, the format or a first change's first-dirty window; no RTL, mailbox-contract or budget-bound change.
Validation plan: firmware unit tests (GoogleTest) and save-harness groups for the burst and the in-flight change, each with planted defects caught by name, branch coverage of new code 100 %; the power-cut tests; on a clean clone of the final head: firmware units and campaigns, `fw_coverage --check`, the verilator-suites shards with the split firmware, elaborate, docs; the CPU service-budget harness at 1x1/1if and 8x8/1if with every row within its bound and the save's windows re-measured (load within 0.70 and 0.75); both split platform images built with timing met and ROM reported; the design page's save worst cases restated from the new measurement.
Blockers: none

[A786] STOP: the 8x8/1if split platform image misses the timing floor at all three directives
Branch: `920-save-burst`, head `54280c94` (code as `f1f7c3e8`; `54280c94` corrects one doc figure).

**The miss.** S9's recipe, one build at a time. Every build has 0 failing endpoints and passes the identity gate.

| 8x8/1if directive | WNS, slow corners | WHS, fast corners |
|---|---|---|
| ExtraPostPlacementOpt (the recipe's) | +0.011 | +0.034 |
| ExtraTimingOpt | +0.171 | +0.014 |
| AltSpreadLogic_high | +0.215 | +0.014 |

- The floor is WNS and WHS >= +0.030 ns at every corner. No build meets it.
- Two builds meet the issue's floors (WNS >= +0.030, WHS >= 0).
- The two hold misses are one path inside `milan_datapath`: `g_aaf_meter.aaf_clock_meter` `s2_ts_r_reg[6]` -> `grp_ts0_r_reg[6]`, on clkout1.
- The setup miss is `KL_mbx_cdc/u_edit/rq_r_reg[80]` -> `milan_datapath/amap_edit_oclaim_expect_r_reg[599]` (CE).
- This change has no RTL. The image differs from the base only in its firmware's bytes: 129,928 B of `rom` where the base has 129,624, in the same 56.0 RAMB36.
- **The base misses identically.** The base's own 8x8/1if image (`659d7687`), built at the recipe's directive, gives the same figures on the same paths: WNS +0.011 and WHS +0.034. The route does not see the firmware's bytes, so the miss is the base's.
- 1x1/1if meets at all three directives. The best is ExtraTimingOpt: WNS +0.133, WHS +0.036.

**Decision needed.** Which of these should apply to the 8x8/1if image?
- accept it at ExtraTimingOpt's or AltSpreadLogic_high's figures;
- run another directive or seed;
- owe the 8x8/1if image's timing to another issue, since the base misses with the same figures.

This round does not choose.

**Everything else, for the decision.**
- **The cause, proved before the fix.** The AECP owner's pending marks held 256 ids. Layout 3 puts the names at id 222 and up, so every name from ordinal 34 on was never delivered to the store. At 1x1/1if those are the five names the rehearsal lost. Three receipts show it at the base:
  - a unit test;
  - the save harness (1x1/1if loses names 34 to 38; at 8x8/1if the CPU traps);
  - the board on its current image: before the cut the store's console bits read backed, nothing dirty, nothing pending, verdict OK.
- **The fix.** `945a1217`: pending bits over layout 3's id space. `c1a24c18`: the ruling's three mechanisms only (a change joins the running capture; the next save starts at the first idle step; a step a pass in passes that took no input).
- **The target, met at both shapes under the held load.**

  | Group | 1x1/1if | 8x8/1if |
  |---|---|---|
  | `save-burst`, latest name to durable after its response | 1,101.7 ms | 1,367.5 ms |
  | `save-burst`, the cut's container | every name | every name |
  | `save-flight`, to durable after its response | 158.5 ms | 657.7 ms |
  | `save-flight`, steps to the next save's erase | 19 (want 19) | 59 (want 59) |

- **The budget harness, every group.**
  - 1x1/1if: exit 0, 0 refusals, 0 of 142,535 passes over the share.
  - 8x8/1if: 0 refusals, 0 of 251,469 passes over the share.
  - At both points the only row misses are the seven held-egress rows, as at the base.
  - 8x8/1if exits 1 on stated-cost lines, as it does at the base. This base keys the statements on the interface count, so 8x8/1if is held to 1x1/1if's. Every such line is within #914's own 8x8/1if statements; the tightest is the polls base, 23,251 of 23,500 cycles.
- **Controls caught by name.** `store-names-past-256-lost` and `store-next-save-waits` at 1x1/1if; `store-step-only-owed` at 8x8/1if. The capture's join has no harness control: without it the burst still meets 5 s (7 saves instead of 6). The store's units hold the join.
- **Gates.**
  - Harness self-test: 0 failures, 251 of 251 mutants caught.
  - Store suite with its mutants: 546 tests at 5 shapes, all 152 planted defects caught.
  - Firmware jobs: 0 failed steps in each (unit, with `fw_coverage --check` passing; the AECP, control and SRP mutant campaigns; verilator; boundary).
  - Docs jobs: 0 failed steps. Elaborate jobs: 0 failed steps, all 8 LiteX simulations passing.
  - Suite sweep: not run before this post, because no CPU range on the shared host came free during the gate run. It runs once one does, and its result goes to the round's record.
  - Load gate: 1x1/1if at 0.516 of 0.70.
  - Python idiom, docs, style and paths checks: pass.
  - Memory ledger: pass.
- **ROM.** Each image grows by 296 to 304 B. The target platform's 8x8 two-interface image is 131,224 B, ledgered at 60.5 RAMB36 as S14 debt (`11860de2`).
- **Ruling item 4.** #919 had no review head; the sync onto it is still open.

[A10] Ruling on the STOP above: **the 8x8/1if timing miss is the base's, not this change's.** Your own route of the base `659d7687` gives identical figures on the same paths, and #919 measured the same. It is now #927 (scope in #927's comments), which is in the flip train ahead of this PR.

For this lane the routes are recorded as "misses at the base, owed to #927", with the figures. It is not a stop and not a debt of this PR. No seeds, no extra directives, and no further routes unless gateware changes after the merge.

The fix meets the ruling's target at both shapes: every name durable within 1.4 s under the held load, against 5 s, with the cause proven at the base first. The 8x8/1if stated-cost lines are #914's per-shape statements, as at the base; record them as such.

Round 2:
- one `--no-ff` merge of dev-soft-core `70f4056f`, with the save groups and affected rows re-measured at both points;
- the remaining gates on a clean clone;
- then REVIEW READY.

The train puts #919 before this PR. The sync onto #919's review head happens once #919 posts REVIEW READY, not now.

[A786] REVIEW READY
Commit: `bd252db1` (branch `920-save-burst`): round 1's `54280c94`, one `--no-ff` merge of `dev-soft-core` `70f4056f` (`d66b4045`, both sides kept), and one docs commit restating the figures as measured on that merge.

**Changed**
- **The cause, proved at the base before any fix.** The AECP owner's pending marks covered 256 ids. Layout 3 puts the names at id 222 and up, so every name from ordinal 34 on never reached the store: at 1x1/1if, the five names the rehearsal lost.
- **`945a1217`:** the pending bits cover layout 3's id space, with a count of the bits set and a static assert.
- **`c1a24c18`:** the ruling's three mechanisms, and nothing else.
  - A change marked during a running capture joins it.
  - The next save starts at the first idle step after the save in flight.
  - A step a pass in passes that took no input, with the step's time left.
- **Tests:**
  - `Nvm.EveryAcknowledgedNameSurvivesTheRealStorePowerCycle`, with AECP mutants;
  - the store's `capture_joins` and `busy_steps` cases, with their mutants;
  - the budget harness's `save-burst` and `save-flight` groups, their grader self-test, and three planted save controls, each caught by name.
- **The merge:** `aecp_nvm.h` keeps this branch's pending-bit words with #901's name runs. The ledger keeps #895's 60.5 for the platform's 8x8/2if image, with #920's 296 B within it. `ctrl_plat` is measured on the merge.

**Validation**
- **CPU budget harness, every group, re-measured on the merge.** The two save groups run first, then the rest in parts, with one `--regrade` a point.
  - 1x1/1if (98 groups): exit 0, 0 refusals, 0 of 132,926 passes over the share, no stated-cost line.
  - 8x8/1if (97 groups): 0 refusals, 0 of 231,039 passes over the share. It exits 1 on stated-cost lines alone, #914's per-shape statements as ruled: the polls base, the most 25,015 cycles against 22,500; an ACMP item, 7,277 against 5,500; a declined offer, 2,338 against 2,000.
  - At both points every row the CPU decides is within its bound. The only misses are the seven held-egress rows behind the 60 ms egress hold, as at the base.
- **The target, at both shapes under the held load:**

  | | 1x1/1if | 8x8/1if |
  |---|---|---|
  | `save-burst`, the latest name durable after its response | 1,107.8 ms | 1,370.3 ms |
  | `save-burst`, saves and the cut | 1 save, every name at the cut | 6 saves, every name at the cut |
  | `save-flight`, durable after its response | 165.0 ms | 663.1 ms |
  | `save-flight`, steps to the next save's erase | 19 (want 19) | 59 (want 59) |
  | `save-starved` and `save-second` against their worst cases | 4,049.1 of 4,070; 6,030.3 of 6,070 ms | 12,448.1 of 12,470; 22,829.6 of 22,870 ms |

- **Self-tests:** the harness's has 0 failures, all 251 mutants caught. The store suite passes 546 tests at 5 shapes and catches all 152 planted defects.
- **rtl-fast firmware jobs** (`d66b4045`): 0 failed steps in each; `verify_wf` reports 0 bad. They cover firmware-unit (with `fw_coverage --check`), the AECP, control and SRP mutant campaigns, verilator and boundary.
- **elaborate** (`d66b4045`) and **docs** (`bd252db1`): 0 failed steps.
- **Load gate:** 1x1/1if at 0.517 of 0.70. The memory ledger, the Python idiom gate and the docs checks pass.
- **ROM:** every image is #901's plus 296 to 304 B, within every entry.
- **Suite sweep at `bd252db1`, four shards:** 65 of 65 suites passed, 0 failed, 0 timed out; 2,713,040 checks, 0 in-suite failures.
- **Round 1's sweep at `54280c94`:** the four suites it could not judge pass alone (`gptp_shadow`, `media_phase`, `milan_dp` and `reboot_ctrl`, rc 0 each).

**Acceptance criteria:** met. Every acknowledged change is durable within 5 s of its response at 1x1/1if and 8x8/1if, under the held load, a burst of every name and a change marked during a save in flight included. Only the ruling's mechanisms are used, with the cause proved first.

**Open risks/questions**
- **The 8x8/1if routes miss at the base, owed to #927.** Per the ruling no route was re-run, and the merge has no gateware change. The figures:
  - the recipe's directive: WNS +0.011, WHS +0.034;
  - ExtraTimingOpt: WNS +0.171, WHS +0.014;
  - AltSpreadLogic_high: WNS +0.215, WHS +0.014.
- **8x8/1if's stated costs** are #914's per-shape statements.
- **The sync onto #919** waits for #919's REVIEW READY.
